source_text: Quis enim hoc, si quid saeculo huic superfuerit aetatis, monumentis credere poterit litterarum exstitisse videlicet hominem, qui crederet et iuraret non esse naturale, quod esset naturale, non esse generationis, quod esset generationis, non pertinere ad condicionem parentum, quod ad aliquos non ob aliud pertineret, nisi quia fuissent parentes? Puto, quod conficta haec magis quam ab ullis defensa mortalibus arbitretur secutura generatio. Hos enim natatus et has nauseas atque hos vomitus vestra natio fidesque perpetitur, qui dicitis: Non possunt parentum peccata ad filios decurrere per naturam, quia res arbitrii seminibus non ligatur, sed peccatum Adae, quod de voluntate conceptum est, transit in omnes homines per naturam, quia res arbitrii seminibus illigata est; non damnat etiam Deus filios pro peccatis parentum, quia summae iniquitatis est, sed damnat Adae posteros propter peccatum parentum, quod nulla potest iustitia vindicari. Non pertinet postremo ad condicionem generationis, quia hi, qui coniuges sunt, fiunt parentes, quod non ob aliud pertinuit ad Adam, nisi quia coniugii lege generavit. Hoccine cursum gubernare est an natare? Hoccine est conficere an nauseare? Hoccine est sumere aliquid solidum an semper evomere? Isdem sermonibus quod negaveris, affirmas, isdem lineis quod affirmaveris, denegas, et irasceris, cur non acquiescamus homini, qui gravi morbo ruptus non potest tenere, quod suscipit.
pass_a_gloss: For who, if any age has survived to this world, will be able to believe by monuments of letters that there existed namely a human who would believe and swear that what was natural is not natural, that what was of generation is not of generation, that what pertained to the condition of parents does not pertain, which pertained to some not for another reason except because they had been parents? I think that a following generation will judge these things more invented than defended by any mortals. For these swimings and these nauseas and these vomitings your nation and faith suffer, who say: Parents' sins cannot run down to sons through nature, because a thing of choice is not bound to seeds, but the sin of Adam, which was conceived from will, passes into all humans through nature, because a thing of choice is bound to seeds; God also does not condemn sons for parents' sins, because it is of highest injustice, but he condemns Adam's posterity on account of the sin of parents, which no justice can vindicate. Finally it does not pertain to the condition of generation, because those who are spouses become parents, which pertained to Adam not for another reason except because he generated by the law of marriage. Is this to govern a course or to swim? Is this to digest or to nauseate? Is this to take something solid or always to vomit? By the same speeches you affirm what you have denied, by the same lines you deny what you have affirmed, and you are angry why we do not acquiesce in a human who, burst by a grave disease, cannot hold what he takes up.

lemmas.lexica: LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will

pass_b_english: If this age has any time left, who will be able to believe the written record that there existed a man who believed and swore that what was natural was not natural, that what belonged to generation did not belong to generation, and that what affected certain people solely because they were parents did not belong to the condition of parents? I think a future generation will consider these claims invented rather than defended by any mortal.

These are the lurchings, nausea, and vomitings your party and belief undergo. You say: Parents’ sins cannot flow to their children through nature, because an act of choice is not bound to reproductive seed; but Adam’s sin, conceived by his will, passes through nature to all people, because an act of choice is bound to reproductive seed. Again: God does not condemn children for their parents’ sins, because that is the height of injustice; but he condemns Adam’s descendants for their parents’ sin, which no justice can defend. Finally: What applied to Adam only because he fathered children under the law of marriage does not belong to the condition of generation by which spouses become parents.

Is this steering a course, or floundering? Is this digesting an argument, or feeling sick? Is this taking in anything solid, or constantly vomiting? In the same words you affirm what you denied; in the same lines you deny what you affirmed. And you are angry that we do not submit to a man so shattered by serious illness that he cannot retain what he takes in (Deuteronomy 24:16)!

choices.why: Julian defends marriage as God's work against the charge that generation transmits sin.
Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: Continues the explicit argument from the law forbidding punishment of parents and children for one another’s sins.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
